land.text: Thessaly, which 'John, Michael's illegitimate son, received' when Michael II's dominions were split in 1267/8

predecessors.note: Medieval Thessaly page: 'r. 1267/8-1289'. The Thessaly page gives 'from 1271' and Cliopatria's row starts in 1272; the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the split at 1268.

land.text: 'Most of Thessaly was taken by the Byzantines following a campaign by Andronikos III Paleologos' (1332); the Byzantines 'established direct control over the northern and eastern part of the region'

successors.note: The Byzantine Empire dossier dates Thessaly's recovery to 1333 and gives it all of Thessaly; the Stephen Gabrielopoulos page says 'northern and eastern part', Medieval Thessaly 'northern and western part' (Ferjancic: 'eastern and central'). The west came under Byzantine control only after Orsini's death three years later (about 1335/6), through the despotate-of-epirus dossier's 1336 loss.

land.text: western Thessaly: John II Orsini of Epirus invaded after Gabrielopoulos' death; per Ferjancic 'the western part remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later' (Medieval Thessaly page)

successors.note: Mirrors despotate-of-epirus /ledger/40 (1332 gain of western Thessaly, same region). The Stephen Gabrielopoulos infobox lists John Orsini (Epirus) and Michael Monomachos (Byzantine Empire) as his successors.

capitals.name: Neopatras (Ypati)
capitals.note: 'From his capital at Neopatras, John I Doukas governed Thessaly as a virtually independent state'; the page names the capital only for John I. Neopatras fell to the Catalans between 1318 and 1325 (this page); 1319 is the Thessaly page's year for the occupation of the south.

capitals.name: Trikala
capitals.note: 'With the loss of Neopatras and the rise of Gabrielopoulos, Trikala became the new political centre of Thessaly'; Trikala heads the estates of Stephen Gabrielopoulos (Stephen page).

rulers.name: John I Doukas
rulers.title: sebastokrator
rulers.note: 'r. 1267/8-1289'; recognised the suzerainty of Michael VIII Palaiologos and received the title of sebastokrator.

rulers.name: Constantine Doukas and Theodore Doukas
rulers.title: joint rulers, sons of John I
rulers.note: Thessaly page: John 'was succeeded by sons Constantine and Theodore'; Medieval Thessaly: both died in 1303.

rulers.name: John II Doukas
rulers.note: Constantine's young son; Guy II de la Roche was regent until 1308 (Medieval Thessaly page); died 1318 without a male heir.

rulers.name: Stephen Gabrielopoulos
rulers.title: sebastokrator, de facto governor of much of Thessaly for the Byzantine emperor
rulers.note: 'ca. 1318 - ca. 1332' in the infobox; died 1332/3. One of three rival magnates (with Signorinos and the Maliasenoi in the east around Volos).

correction.text: Thessaly as John I Doukas held it from 1267/8 (Cliopatria's first shape, 1272)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1268-1271: Cliopatria's row begins in 1272 but 'John, Michael's illegitimate son' received Thessaly when Michael II's dominions were split (1267/8, r. 1267/8-1289). The Thessaly page dates the despotate from 1271. The 1272 shape is used for the earlier years.

Years only: the shape (14,407 km2) is valid 1272-1318. The infobox of the Thessaly article is the modern region and gives no medieval area to compare. Conflict between pages: the Thessaly article says the despotate 'extended to Acarnania and Aetolia' (1271-1318), but the Medieval Thessaly article names no such land (the Aetolia-Acarnania conquest there is Nikephoros Orsini's after 1355) and Cliopatria's bbox stops at 38.87 N and 21.36 E, leaving Acarnania and Aetolia to the Despotate of Epirus (21 shapes 1206-1481). The shape is kept; see notes.

correction.text: Thessaly without Neopatras and the south occupied by the Catalans in 1319

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1319-1325: 'In 1319 the Almogavars occupied southern Thessaly' and formed the Duchy of Neopatria; Medieval Thessaly says the Catalans took Neopatras, the capital, between 1318 and 1325. A 25 km radius around Neopatras is removed from the shape; the places taken by 1325 (Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron, Vitrinitsa) follow in thessaly_1326.

correction.text: Thessaly without the Catalan Duchy of Neopatras

keyframe_review.note: 14,184 km2 (-222 km2 on 1272): 'Between 1318 and 1325, the Catalans took Neopatras, Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron, and Vitrinitsa', so the small shrinkage is explained, but the Catalan Company's 1326 shape still overlaps this one at its northern tip, so the overlap is subtracted. The page shows a divided country in these years: 'three rival magnates' in the centre (Stephen Gabrielopoulos at Trikala, Signorinos, the Maliasenoi in the east around Volos) and 'the north came under control of the Byzantines from Thessalonica'; Cliopatria draws one Thessalian state to 1332, which is kept as the most the pages support (see notes). The John II Doukas page (read after review) adds only that after 1318 'much of northwestern Thessaly came under the control of' Stephen Gabrielopoulos and the Catalans took the southernmost areas; it does not delimit the Maliasenoi, Signorinos or the Byzantine north, so the one-state shape stays.

region.text: Thessaly, received by John, 'Michael's illegitimate son'

ledger.note: 1268: John I Doukas takes Thessaly at the partition of Michael II's dominions. 'On Michael II's death, his dominions were split': John 'received Thessaly' and Nikephoros Epirus proper (r. 1267/8-1289); 'From his capital at Neopatras, John I Doukas governed Thessaly as a virtually independent state.' The Thessaly page says 'From 1271 to 1318 Thessaly was an independent despotate' and Cliopatria starts in 1272; the year is the page's 1267/8 and the region is the researcher's reading of 'Thessaly'.

1318: John II Doukas dies without a male heir and the Doukas despotate ends. 'In 1318, with the death of John II, Thessalian independence came to an end.' Stephen Gabrielopoulos, 'sometime between 1318 and 1325', acknowledged Byzantine suzerainty and became 'de facto governor of much of Thessaly on behalf of the Byzantine emperor' (Stephen page); the other magnates, the Byzantine north and the Catalan south are described in the Medieval Thessaly page. The Byzantine Empire dossier should carry the overlordship.

1319: the Catalan Company occupies southern Thessaly. 'In 1319 the Almogavars occupied southern Thessaly' and formed the Duchy of Neopatria; 'When John Doukas died in 1318, the southern part of Thessaly was quickly captured by the Catalans of Athens' (Medieval Thessaly). The Company had plundered Thessaly in 1306-1310 and in 1310 'occupied a series of forts in the south' (Thessaly page).

1319: the seat moves from Neopatras to Trikala. 'With the loss of Neopatras and the rise of Gabrielopoulos, Trikala became the new political centre of Thessaly.' The page gives no year for the move; the loss of Neopatras (1319) is used.

region.text: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa (the growth of the Catalan Company's 1326 shape over its 1314 shape)

ledger.note: 1325: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa are Catalan. 'Between 1318 and 1325, the Catalans took Neopatras, Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron, and Vitrinitsa.' The page gives a span, not a year for each; 1325 is its closing year and matches the change in Cliopatria's shapes at 1326.

region.text: 'Most of Thessaly': the northern and eastern part, taken as the Larissa disc within Thessaly (Stephen Gabrielopoulos page: 'the northern and eastern part of the region'; Ferjancic: 'eastern and central Thessaly')

ledger.note: 1332: the Byzantines take most of Thessaly. 'In 1332, most of Thessaly was taken by the Byzantines following a campaign by Andronikos III Paleologos' (Thessaly page; 'most', not all). Stephen Gabrielopoulos died 1332/3 and his heirs quarrelled; the Byzantines 'established direct control over the northern and eastern part of the region' (Stephen page), 'the northern and western part' (Medieval Thessaly, 'c. 1333'), 'eastern and central Thessaly' (Ferjancic); the north and east reading is used because it agrees with the Stephen page and leaves the west to Epirus (next event). The year is the Thessaly page's and the region is the researcher's reading (confidence 2); the Byzantine Empire dossier dates the same gain 1333 and gives it all of Thessaly (to be split by its owner).

region.text: western Thessaly, which 'remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later' (Ferjancic, Medieval Thessaly page); the complement of the Larissa disc, as in the despotate-of-epirus dossier

ledger.note: 1332: John II Orsini of Epirus takes the west. Gabrielopoulos' heirs quarrelled, 'leading to an invasion by the Epirote ruler John II Orsini' (Stephen page); John II Orsini 'tried to take advantage of the situation and seize his lands', and per Ferjancic 'the western part remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later' (Medieval Thessaly), 'when this area too came under Byzantine control' (c. 1335/6: neither page gives the year of his death). Mirrors despotate-of-epirus /ledger/40 (1332 gain, same region); the Epirote part passes to the Byzantines in 1336 (despotate-of-epirus /ledger/41), after Thessaly's end.

region.text: the Thessaly of Cliopatria's last shape, 1326-1332

ledger.note: 1332: Thessaly ends. The last ruler of the Doukas land, Stephen Gabrielopoulos, 'ca. 1318 - ca. 1332' (died 1332/3); the north and east pass to the Byzantines under Andronikos III and the west to John II Orsini of Epirus (the two losses above); 'With Orsini's death three years later, all of Thessaly came under Byzantine control' (Stephen page). The dissolve region is Cliopatria's last shape; counterpart is the Byzantine Empire, which received most of it. The Byzantine Empire dossier dates the recovery to 1333, the Epirus dossier the annexation by Orsini to 1332.

wars.name: Byzantine-Thessalian wars under John I Doukas
wars.outcome: No border change on the page: John I won the Battle of Neopatras with Athenian aid against an army under John Palaiologos (c. 1273-75, date disputed); a Byzantine expedition in 1277 failed; in 1282 Michael VIII 'campaigned against John, but fell ill and died on the way'.
wars.note: John nominally recognised Michael VIII's suzerainty and held the title of sebastokrator but 'maintained a consistent anti-Palaiologan stance'.

wars.name: Thessalian invasion of Epirus
wars.outcome: 'In 1295 the brothers invaded Epirus themselves and seized Naupaktos, but no further gains appear to have been made.' The page does not say how long Naupaktos was held; the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the 1294-95 events from the Nikephoros I page. The Nikephoros I page (read after review) does not name Naupaktos but says the ruler of Thessaly intervened in 1294-95 to seize 'mostly the fortresses' that Nikephoros had handed over as Thamar's dowry and that 'Eventually most of these were recovered by the Angevins and peace was restored in 1296', so any seizure lasted at most to 1296.
wars.note: Naupaktos lies outside Cliopatria's Thessaly bbox, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Catalan Company raids on Thessaly
wars.outcome: The Company 'plundered Thessaly' in 1306-1310 and in 1310 'occupied a series of forts in the south' (Thessaly page); 'In early 1309 the Catalan Company ... crossed from Macedonia into Thessaly' (Medieval Thessaly). No border change is drawn: the forts' fate is not on the pages.

wars.name: Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly

zones.text: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa (the growth of the Catalan Company's 1326 shape over its 1314 shape)

wars.outcome: The Catalans take Neopatras in 1319 and Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa by 1325 and form the Duchy of Neopatras.

wars.name: Byzantine and Epirote partition of Thessaly

zones.text: western Thessaly, which 'remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later' (Ferjancic, Medieval Thessaly page); the complement of the Larissa disc, as in the despotate-of-epirus dossier

wars.outcome: Andronikos III takes most of Thessaly (the north and east, per the Stephen page); John II Orsini of Epirus seizes the west; all Thessaly is Byzantine after Orsini's death three years later (about 1335/6).
wars.note: Zone is the western part held by Epirus 1332-c.1336, the one stretch the Byzantines and Epirus disputed. Ferjancic (cited on the Medieval Thessaly page) holds that the western part stayed Epirote until Orsini's death; Kantakouzenos claims the old Epirote-Thessalian border (the Pindus) was restored.

certainty.note: Thirteenth- and fourteenth-century Thessalian frontiers are named by towns and castles only; the 1318-1332 division among magnates, Byzantines and Catalans is not delimited by any page.

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from three pages (budget 1-2; one over, taken to settle the start date, the capital and 1318-1332). Start: 1268 (Medieval Thessaly '1267/8') against the Thessaly article's 1271 and Cliopatria's 1272; the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the split at 1268. End: the Thessaly page says 'Thessalian independence came to an end' in 1318, yet Stephen Gabrielopoulos ruled western Thessaly 'ca. 1318 - ca. 1332' under Byzantine suzerainty and Cliopatria runs the row to 1332, so 1332 is kept as the end with 1318 as a break (rename); the 1318-1332 map is really a patchwork (Byzantines in the north 'from Thessalonica', the Maliasenoi around Volos, Signorinos, the Catalans in the south) that the pages do not delimit; a gap-filler could split it. Page conflicts: the Thessaly article says the despotate 'extended to Acarnania and Aetolia'; Medieval Thessaly does not; Cliopatria leaves them to Epirus; shape kept. Extent of the 1332 Byzantine takeover: 'northern and eastern' (Stephen page), 'northern and western' (Medieval Thessaly), 'eastern and central' (Ferjancic) and the year 1332 (Thessaly) against 1333 (Byzantine dossier, Medieval Thessaly c. 1333). Overlordship for the Byzantine Empire dossier (the pages give no start year for the first): John I recognised Michael VIII's suzerainty (sebastokrator); John's widow 'was compelled to recognize the suzerainty' of Andronikos II (c. 1289-90); John II recognised it c. 1315 and married Irene Palaiologina; Stephen Gabrielopoulos acknowledged it between 1318 and 1325. Not settled: how long Naupaktos was held after 1295 (no ledger event, since Cliopatria's shape excludes it); Guy II de la Roche as regent for John II until 1308; who held Larissa. No medieval area on any page, so the area comparison could not be made. Gazetteer lacks Neopatras (Ypati), Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron, Vitrinitsa and Trikala; coordinates are used. Review fixes 2026-10-19: the 1332 loss now goes to the Byzantines for the north and east only (the Larissa 50 km disc within Thessaly, confidence 2) and a second 1332 loss gives western Thessaly to the despotate-of-epirus (the complement of that disc, mirroring despotate-of-epirus /ledger/40, confidence 2); despotate-of-epirus is added to identity.successors and the war entry now runs 1332-1336 with the western zone. Re-read: Thessaly page 'In 1332, most of Thessaly was taken by the Byzantines'; Stephen page 'northern and eastern part', Orsini invasion, 'With Orsini's death three years later, all of Thessaly came under Byzantine control'; Medieval Thessaly 'northern and western part', Ferjancic 'eastern and central' with 'the western part remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later'. I follow the Stephen page and Ferjancic (north and east Byzantine, west Epirote) because the Epirus dossier already uses the Larissa complement; the Medieval Thessaly sentence 'northern and western part' contradicts that and is not followed. The byzantine-empire dossier's /ledger/172 (1333 gain of all Thessaly from thessaly) still needs the same split: Larissa disc in 1332/3, the west only after Orsini's death (about 1335/6, the Epirus dossier's 1336); that dossier belongs to eu-05 (another part). The 1295 and 1318-1332 thin items were tried on the Nikephoros I and John II Doukas pages (see sources); neither settles them.
